the sensitivity of the source model to initial electron-beam energy and radial distribution.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the target subsource is the only one that should be adjusted when the initial electron beam parameters change.

the electron-beam parameters have a significant influence on the target subsource, but only a negligible influence on primary collimator and the flattening filter subsource.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a MC source model can be constructed for a specific electron-beam condition and then scaled for other electron-beam conditions.
MC source models are robust to the initial electron beam energy and radial distribution changes.
the electron-beam parameters can be adjusted in a MC source-model without the need to recalculate the primary collimator or flattening filter subsource distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the target subsource is the most sensitive to the changes in the electron-beam parameters.

the target subsource can be used to account for a change of the initial electron energy and radial distribution, and that the relative intensity and spectra of the primary collimation and flattening filter subsource distributions can be accounted for using a simple scaling factor.

MC-based dose calculations for radiotherapy can be performed accurately and efficiently by using a simple source model, with only the target subsource requiring adjustment when the accelerator parameters change.
